fills.reason: Searched app sources for getExternalStorage*/getExternalFilesDir/getExternalCacheDir/MediaStore and WRITE/MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE: none in the app module or its manifest; the only hit is a test-only screenshot rule in release_tests.
A hardcoded secret string is used as the HMAC-SHA256 key that authenticates UDP/TCP ping packets sent to VPN servers; anyone extracting it from the APK can forge authenticated pings.

evidence.detail: HMAC key hardcoded as a string constant.
The constant is turned into the HMAC key used to sign ping data.

fills.reason: Direct android.util.Log calls go through utils/Log.java, which only logs when BuildConfig.DEBUG; remaining Log calls log exceptions/metadata. A search of ProtonLogger calls for token/password/key/email found only messages saying restrictions exist, not their values.
The only WebView (OssLicensesActivity) enables JavaScript but never calls setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs(true), so the fail condition (all three) is not met.

OssLicensesActivity enables JavaScript and loads a bundled asset but does not set setAllowFileAccessFromFileURLs/setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs (defaults false since API 16; minSdk 26 in build-logic AndroidConfig).
No addJavascriptInterface or @JavascriptInterface anywhere in app sources; the one JS-enabled WebView exposes no bridge.

The app's own text fields (bug-report email, profile name/URL, DNS, split-tunnel IPs, search) set no non-caching keyboard options; the only personal one is the bug-report email field. Whether that counts as sensitive is a human call. Login/password fields live in the external me.proton.core library, not in this project.

evidence.detail: Email input field with default keyboard options.

fills.reason: No FLAG_SECURE / setRecentsScreenshotEnabled anywhere in app sources. Screens show account info and the TV sign-in (session fork) confirmation; whether these count as sensitive enough to need screenshot protection is a human decision.
Notifications show VPN state, server/traffic strings, error messages and upsell text; no PII, OTPs or credentials are put in setContentTitle/setContentText.

No password, PIN or OTP input fields exist in the app's own sources (sign-in UI comes from the external me.proton.core library; TV sign-in uses a QR/code flow). App text fields are for email, names, URLs, DNS and IPs.

No overlay protection (filterTouchesWhenObscured, onFilterTouchEventForSecurity, FLAG_WINDOW_IS_OBSCURED, setHideOverlayWindows) anywhere. The session-fork confirmation, which grants another device a session and can be opened by any app through the protonvpn://session-fork deep link, only has a time-since-resume delay, which does not stop overlays.

evidence.detail: Confirm-sign-in button with no touch filtering for obscured windows.
Only protection is a minimum time since onResume.

fills.reason: Internal broadcasts/intents name the component (QuickTileActionReceiver, NotificationActionReceiver, activity classes) or set the package (WidgetManager); no implicit internal intents found.
Intents carrying extras are explicit (Intent(context, X::class.java) or launch intents for the own package); the only action-based intent sets the app's own package and has no sensitive extras.
Every PendingIntent.getActivity/getBroadcast in the app uses FLAG_IMMUTABLE, and base intents are explicit (component class, own launch intent, or setPackage).
The only https deep link (account.proton.me/vpn/tv/code/) is declared in an intent-filter with android:autoVerify="true"; Digital Asset Links verification itself was not checked.

protonvpn://refresh-account only triggers a plan refresh and uses no parameters; protonvpn://session-fork extracts a code checked for scheme/host and length 8 before going to the backend, and the user must confirm.

TvMainActivity and the launcher aliases are normal entry points; SessionForkConfirmation requires user confirmation. However the exported MainActivity aliases accept an explicit intent with a glance-action data URI plus extras and start a VPN connection to a recent entry without user interaction. Whether letting any app change the VPN connection counts as sensitive is a human call.

evidence.detail: Exported activity routes any intent with the glance-action scheme to the widget action handler.
Handler connects the VPN based on intent extras.

fills.reason: The four exported receivers are Glance app-widget receivers (TrackedWidgetReceiver subclasses with no custom onReceive) that only handle APPWIDGET_UPDATE/LOCALE_CHANGED to redraw widgets; the action receiver WidgetActionBroadcastReceiver is not exported.
kotlin.random.Random is used only for jitter delays, metrics sampling, port/server choice and profile colors; no keys, IVs, tokens or passwords come from it.
No security values are derived from time; the wall-clock time in ServerPing is a timestamp inside the HMAC'd ping, not a secret.
No KeyGenerator/KeyPairGenerator usage in app sources (searched app/src/main); key generation in the legacy ProtonPreferences is done by the Tozny AesCbcWithIntegrity library.
The only Cipher.getInstance is AES/GCM/NoPadding (AssetManager); ProtonPreferences uses AesCbcWithIntegrity (AES-CBC+HMAC). No DES/3DES/RC4/Blowfish.
No ECB or bare "AES" transformation; the only Cipher transformation is AES/GCM/NoPadding.
No KeyGenParameterSpec or KeyPairGenerator in app sources (searched app/src/main for both).
getInstance calls (Cipher, Mac, MessageDigest) name no security provider.

No BiometricPrompt/BiometricManager usage in app/src (searched all source sets).

No SSLContext.getInstance with old TLS versions, setEnabledProtocols or OkHttp ConnectionSpec in app sources; HTTP stack is configured in the external me.proton.core network library (not inspected).
No http:// URLs in app Kotlin/Java; the only ones are license links in bundled OSS-license assets and XML namespaces, and the network security config forbids cleartext.
No SSLSocket usage in app sources (release_tests is a test module).
No custom X509TrustManager/checkServerTrusted in the app module; the trust-all manager found is in release_tests (test module, not shipped).
No HostnameVerifier implementation in app sources.

Hardening: no ProviderInstaller.installIfNeeded(Async) call in any app source set, including the google flavor. That meets the fail condition, but a missing call has no file:line to cite, and non-Google flavors can't use GMS anyway.
minSdk is 26 (build-logic AndroidConfig.MIN_SDK_VERSION) and 25 for the Amazon flavor (build.gradle minSdkVersionAmazon), both >= 24.
The network security config has only a base-config with cleartextTrafficPermitted=false and no trust-anchors including certificates src="user".

The network security config has no pin-set, but the app pins API connections in code through SPKI pins handed to the Proton core network stack. Whether code pinning covers every endpoint you control needs a dynamic check (MASTG-TEST-0244).

evidence.detail: Default SPKI pins used for the API.

fills.reason: WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled(true) is only called inside if (BuildConfig.DEBUG).
No WebViewClient, shouldOverrideUrlLoading or shouldInterceptRequest in app sources; the one WebView only shows a bundled license page.
No EnableSafeBrowsing meta-data in the manifest and no setSafeBrowsingEnabled(false) in code.
The project has no native build of its own; the native libraries come from dependencies (for example WireGuard). PIC can only be checked on the built APK's .so files.
Stack canaries can only be checked on the native libraries in the built APK, which comes from dependencies; not possible from source.
The app checks Build.VERSION.SDK_INT in several places (e.g. QuickTileService, AndroidUtils).
Needs an SBOM of the resolved (including transitive) dependencies; Ward's direct-dependency check is separate.

getSerializableExtra is used only in non-exported activities/receivers (NotificationActionReceiver, NoVpnPermissionActivity, UpgradeDialogActivity, split-tunnel settings), mostly with typed getters; exported MainActivity reads only boolean/long extras.
Deciding which locally stored values drive security decisions (plan tier, settings) and whether they're re-validated by the backend needs a broader review than a source scan.
The app defines no ContentProvider subclass and the manifest exports no providers.
A backend force-update error triggers the core ForceUpdateActivity and logs the user out (LogoutOnForceUpdate); the Google flavor also prompts on stale versions.
signingConfigs don't disable v2/v3 signing (no v2SigningEnabled false), so AGP's defaults sign with v2+; minSdk 26.

Key size can only be read from the signed APK. Note: the release build type in source is signed with signingConfigs.debug (androiddebugkey); confirm that production builds are re-signed with the real release key.

evidence.detail: Release build type uses the debug signing config.

fills.reason: No StrictMode references in app sources or build-logic.
Debug symbols in native binaries can only be checked on the built APK's .so files.
The app has a root check (isDeviceRooted) whose result is reported in Sentry events; it is used only for telemetry, not to change behavior (how well it works is out of scope).

Hardening: no Debug.isDebuggerConnected, TracerPid or ptrace-based debugger detection in app sources. That meets the fail condition, but a missing call has no file:line to cite, and native libraries weren't inspected.
Release has minifyEnabled true (R8 renaming); whether that's enough obfuscation for security-relevant code needs the decompiled APK.
Native obfuscation can only be judged on the built native libraries.
Neither app/build.gradle's release buildType nor the build-logic convention plugins set debuggable/isDebuggable, and the manifest has no android:debuggable.
The only dangerous permission is POST_NOTIFICATIONS, needed for the VPN status/foreground-service notification and connection alerts.
The app passes a persistent installation ID to the Sentry SDK as the user ID (crash reporting is on by default, opt-out). This identifier must be declared in the Data safety form.

evidence.detail: Installation ID sent to Sentry as the user identifier.
